chapter: Charlie Johnson, Willie Gant and the late 1920s
title: Tommy Ladnier's retreat from music
summary: Ladnier, like Ward Pinkett, withdrew from music, and Caldwell thinks Hawkins had the same disgust.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: I used to go see Tommy all the time. He remind me a lot of Ward. Seem like he got in some kind of this way of just -- I

don't know just -- he forgot about music, seems he didn't like it. I said, Tommy, come on, let's go some places. Hap, I don't (unintelligible). [I mean from Chicago, but he came from Chicago.] And it seem like whether it was a woman's thing upset him or what, he was just cool, you know, him and Ward the same way. But he didn't drink. He wasn't no drinker, Tommy wasn't.
Well, you don't think he (unintelligible) sort of got disgusted with the music -- with the music business maybe.
I think that's what happened to Hawk too.
